A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Video Depth Anything. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary sections are readable and support reliable comparison, including v3's added material.

before.justification: V1 reports original video and image depth evaluations, latency measurements, ablations and qualitative application results, including supplementary Table 7.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations of public-data-only training variants and wild-video point-cloud examples.

M1.justification: The encoder, temporal head, losses and key-frame stitching method are retained. Section 3.3 clarifies first-frame anchoring while retaining Figure 3's parameters. The added -Syn models use different training configurations, without changing the architecture or objectives.

E1.justification: Figure 13 extends point-cloud reconstruction evaluation from KITTI to three wild videos from DAVIS. DAVIS already appeared in depth and stereo-video examples, but this reconstruction scenario is new. The underlying training datasets and depth benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The benchmark baselines remain unchanged, and Figure 13 uses the same point-cloud comparators as Figure 12: DepthCrafter and DepthAnyVideo. The -Syn rows are training variants of the proposed model; MoGe supplies calibration rather than serving as an evaluated depth baseline.

E3.justification: V3 adds single-stage training configurations using synthetic videos and unlabeled images for the -Syn models, alongside the retained two-stage models. Figure 13 introduces a three-video procedure using MoGe on each first frame to obtain camera intrinsics and scale/shift alignment. Existing benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds comparisons of two public-data-only training variants, and Figure 13 adds wild-video reconstruction case studies. The existing temporal-loss, inference-strategy, window-size and image-distillation ablations are retained without changed results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional results do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds two -Syn rows; for example, VDA-L-Syn reports ScanNet AbsRel 0.087 and δ1 0.933. Original models' AbsRel, δ1 and TAE entries remain unchanged, while reported ranks change, including VDA-L from 1.6 to 1.7. Figure 13 adds qualitative findings of more regular point clouds.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(5), the OPW critique, stable-error and temporal-gradient loss reasoning, and alignment mathematics are retained. No mathematical definition, proof or formal assumption is substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about consistent arbitrarily long video depth, temporal-gradient supervision, generalization and computational efficiency. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The limitations section changes the description from publicly available datasets without special curation to primarily publicly available datasets. Section 3.3 additionally explains first-frame anchoring as supporting long-video consistency. The existing data-quantity and streaming-video limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 documents first-frame anchoring, the -Syn models' single-stage training and MoGe-based calibration. The introduction changes 550K training frames to 730K, accounting for the additional 180K binocular frames already disclosed in v1's appendix; this does not establish newly added training data. The project link is unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds MoGe as reference 36 for Figure 13's geometric calibration. The related-work discussion and broader research positioning remain unchanged; subsequent citation-number changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: Localized additions clarify key-frame inference, single-image evaluation, training variants and applications, with revised training-data wording. Most prose and the overall section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two rows and an expanded caption, Figure 13 adds point-cloud panels, and Figures 2-3 receive graphical revisions. Existing figures are retained with some resizing and reflow. Moving Table 5 to the other column removes its overlap with Table 4's caption.

improvement.justification: The public-data-only evaluations, clearer training and inference documentation, additional reconstruction examples and corrected table overlap modestly improve evidence and readability. Reporting remains imperfect: Table 7 still lists 0.55M training frames, and Table 1's revised VDA-L rank of 1.7 does not match the 2.2 mean rank implied by its displayed δ1 values under the rule reproducing v1's ranks. These issues limit the gain without overturning the retained primary results.
